newsitem.title: INDIA: India Shipping Corp outlines buying plans.
newsitem.headline: India Shipping Corp outlines buying plans.

text.p: State-run Shipping Corp of India (SCI) said on Tuesday that two crude oil tankers which the government has authorised it to buy are part of a plan to purchase 44 vessels over the next five years.
The government on Monday approved SCI's proposal to buy the two tankers from South Korea's Halla Engineering and Heavy Industries Ltd, an affiliate of the Halla Group, for $42.10 million each.
Later on Monday the Surface Transport Ministry announced that SCI planned to buy 44 vessels with a total dry weight tonnage (DWT) of 1.95 million during the ninth Five-Year Plan ending in 2002.
SCI director K.K. Palit told Reuters on Tuesday that among the 44 vessels, the company planned to buy two product tankers from South Korea's Hyundai Heavy Industries Co Ltd.
"The 44 include the oil tankers to be bought from Halla Engineering and two product tankers from Hyundai," Palit said.
He said SCI had already placed orders with Hyundai for the two product tankers with 30,000 DWT each.

"We signed the contract with Hyundai for one on May 1," Palit said. "For the other, also with the same tonnage, the letter of intent was sent yesterday to Hyundai and the agreement will be signed in the course of time."
The Surface Transport Ministry said the total cost of buying the 44 vessels would be about 45 billion rupees ($1.26 billion).
The ministry said the two oil tankers are expected to be delivered to SCI in the second quarter of 1999.
Palit said the remaining 40 vessels would include oil tankers, product tankers, bulk carriers, gas carriers and container vessels.
"It will be done through global tendering but it will be gradually done," Palit said. He declined to give details.
SCI currently has a fleet of 29 crude oil tankers with DWT of 2.74 million tonnes.
In May, SCI reported net profit of 2.57 billion rupees for 1996/97 (April-March), down from 3.23 billion in the previous year.
SCI attributed the decline to the fact it had paid tax for the first time under the minimum alternate tax provision, and also to lower freight levels. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
